tracking_records.title: AccelForge: Comprehensive Modeling and Co-Design Framework for AI Accelerators
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / accelerator modeling and co-design
tracking_records.why: AccelForge unifies device, circuit, architecture, workload, and mapping models, with composable models and fast mappers that evaluate designs orders of magnitude faster in computer and human time than prior workflows.

tracking_records.title: Building py-kvcache: A Performance Characterization of External KV Caching for vLLM with NVMe SSDs
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / KV cache / NVMe offload
tracking_records.why: Scheduler-aware asynchronous NVMe KV preloading overlaps disk reads with waiting/compute. At 80k tokens disk loading is 2.0x faster than LMCache; with GPU/CPU/disk tiers enabled it is 1.23x faster and within about 4% of native vLLM KV Offload.

tracking_records.title: LOCUS: Task-Aware Low-Rank Post-Training for Token-Efficient Language Generation
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / efficient reasoning / output-token reduction
tracking_records.why: Selects a task-aware low-rank post-training subspace that minimizes output-token cost under a utility constraint while updating only 0.24-0.28% of parameters. Continuation length falls by up to 39.84% on Pythia-2.8B and 14.87-17.58% on Qwen2.5-3B without material change in the internal preference diagnostic.

tracking_records.title: Structured Transforms for Low-Overhead Quantization of Language Models
tracking_records.topic: quantization / low-overhead LLM compression
tracking_records.why: Replacing dense random orthogonal transforms with sign-randomized DCT reduces each quantization iteration from O(N^2) to O(N log N), removes multi-restart k-means initialization, and shows favorable wall-clock scaling while producing native-2-bit-suited factors.

tracking_records.title: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent runtime harness
tracking_records.why: Cross-instance failure diagnosis accelerates self-evolving runtime-harness training. The paper reports up to 1.84x harness-training speedup while improving resulting reasoning accuracy by 18.56%.

tracking_records.title: OmniKVQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Omni-LLMs
tracking_records.topic: KV cache/long-context / quantization / multimodal serving
tracking_records.why: Training-free modality-aware KV quantization handles temporal key drift and heterogeneous value geometry in audio-video-text caches. Enables 2-bit KV caches on Qwen2.5-Omni/Qwen3-Omni and provides a fused Triton decode kernel that never materializes dense FP16 KV.

tracking_records.title: Entwine: Coordinating Tiled Computation and Fine-Grained Communication across GPUs
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / GPU communication overlap / tensor parallelism
tracking_records.why: Coordinates tile computation order, fine-grained SM communication, and SM allocation. Across tensor-parallel LLM workloads it achieves 1.232x geomean speedup, up to 1.433x, over cuBLAS+NCCL and beats state-of-the-art overlap baselines by 3.1-9.8% geomean.

tracking_records.title: Memory as Plans: World-Action Modeling with Memory-Grounded Planning
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / memory and long-horizon runtime
tracking_records.why: MaP-WAM converts long multimodal episodic memory into compact plans, keeps executor context length fixed, and enables KV caching in planning and execution. It reaches 83.3% RMBench and 78.0% real-robot success while maintaining approximately constant executor inference latency as history grows.

tracking_records.title: Characterizing Job Power Elasticity for Power-Flexible AI Training
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / datacenter power scheduling
tracking_records.why: A systematic characterization of LLM-training power elasticity over 131 H200 runs plus validation and H100 matches. PFI-aware allocation under a 30% power reduction recovers about 1.5k tokens/s per job, 63% of the gap between equal allocation and an oracle.

tracking_records.title: Calibration-Aware Uncertainty Cascades for Efficient Heterogeneous Model Collaboration
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / adaptive model routing
tracking_records.why: Post-hoc calibrated confidence creates a common reliability scale across heterogeneous models. Across six language benchmarks it avoids about 47% of strong-model calls while improving average accuracy, and reduces measured GFLOPs by up to 57% on image classification.

tracking_records.title: PATTON: Enabling Commodity PIM for Production LLM Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / KV cache / PIM accelerator runtime
tracking_records.why: Integrates production KV lifecycle management with commodity PIM using hierarchical granule allocation and a Commit Zone for efficient Value writes. Reports 1.95x average speedup and 4.83x energy efficiency over evaluated baselines without PIM processing-unit changes.

tracking_records.title: VikingRAG: Accurate and Token-efficient Retrieval-augmented Generation over Structured Documents
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / token-efficient RAG serving
tracking_records.why: Directory-aware semantic retrieval, trace reuse, and adaptive escalation cut token use to 11.6%-51.9% of prior systems, and to 5.1%-32.5% with experience-edge reuse and escalation, while retaining competitive accuracy.

tracking_records.title: Memory Compression for High-Fanout Agent Sandboxes
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / sandbox memory / runtime compression
tracking_records.why: AgentZip exploits template-relative and cross-sandbox redundancy and aligns compression with LLM waiting periods. It cuts sandbox-owned memory by up to 8.7x versus 2.1x for Linux; restore prefetching and execution-aware scheduling reduce aggressive-compression slowdown from as high as 3.1x to 1.40x while retaining nearly all memory savings.

tracking_records.title: A Voice-Interactive Multi-Agent System for Smart Operating Rooms: Architecture Design and Key Technologies
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / agent systems / KV cache / streaming execution
tracking_records.why: Implements Qwen3-27B with llama.cpp/SGLang and combines byte-level KV-prefix warming, streaming partial-JSON parsing with early parallel execution, and progressive skill-prompt disclosure. Prefix reuse reduces recomputation from about 500 ms to tens of milliseconds and streaming execution cuts end-to-end latency by about 30%. Domain deployment is surgical, but the runtime techniques are directly reusable LLM-serving mechanisms.

tracking_records.title: REVA: Reusable Evidence View Aggregation for Context-Efficient RAG Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / RAG / context compression
tracking_records.why: Mines historical generator attention into reusable document-keyed evidence views instead of running an online compressor per query. Cuts compression overhead by 5.3-15.6x, adds under 40 ms latency, and improves generation quality by 1.0-5.8 points.

tracking_records.title: FlexComp: One Model for Every Ratio in Context Compression
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / context compression / adaptive inference
tracking_records.why: Any-ratio context compressor chooses memory budget per input via cascade routing or a lightweight predictor. Preserves over 98% mild-ratio accuracy at up to 266x average compression; at serving batch sizes it cuts context KV cache by 50% and improves decoding throughput by 47%.

tracking_records.title: LILA: Calibration-Free Structured Pruning of Large Language Models via Latent Spectral Geometry
tracking_records.topic: sparsity/pruning / LLM compression / calibration-free structured pruning
tracking_records.why: Closed-form spectral neuron scoring requires no calibration data, gradients, training, or auxiliary policy network at pruning time. At 25% sparsity LILA beats PruneNet by 1.57 pp zero-shot accuracy and calibrated SliceGPT by up to 6.0 pp; NTK analysis reports 22x lower functional distortion than random pruning.

tracking_records.title: Phase-Decoupled, Model-Calibrated Power Control for Disaggregated LLM Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / PD disaggregation / energy efficiency
tracking_records.why: Phase-specific power control calibrates prefill and decode independently under latency/SLO guards. On 8x B200 with Qwen3-Coder-480B it improves tokens/J by 20.4% at only 3.5% mean end-to-end latency cost and a three-day run saves 32.3% electricity for a lane pair.

tracking_records.title: Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / persistent memory / production harness
tracking_records.why: Environment-probing memory curation needs no retraining and leaves the task agent/retriever/memory format unchanged. In a GitHub Copilot SDK harness, CLBench pass rate rises 39%->73%, queries fall 8.8->4.7, and task-agent cost falls $3.38->$1.68; APEX tool calls fall 16-75%.

tracking_records.title: EMMI: Edge Multi-Modal Intelligence for Communication-Efficient MLLM Inference via Fused Representation Compression
tracking_records.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / edge-cloud split inference
tracking_records.why: Representation-centric edge/server MLLM inference compresses fused multimodal state before transmission. The paper reports 32x lower communication payload with comparable downstream accuracy and up to 3.4x lower estimated end-to-end latency under bandwidth-constrained edge conditions.

tracking_records.title: BEACON: A Versatile Accelerator for Computational Pathology Applications
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / accelerator architecture / AI+X
tracking_records.why: Extends a baseline systolic AI accelerator with small flexible datapath and operator-support changes. The added logic grows chiplet area by only 1.1x while delivering over an order of magnitude higher throughput than CPU/GPU baselines on the multi-stage workload; retained for reusable accelerator-polymorphism lineage beyond the specific pathology application.

tracking_records.title: Fengshui: Demystifying Chiplet Ecosystem and Bespoke Neural Network Accelerator Codesign
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / chiplet accelerator codesign
tracking_records.why: Operator-level disaggregation and chiplet-pool co-design with physical validation. Eight selected chiplets achieve 93.0% EDP and 97.8% EDPC reductions versus homogeneous accelerators; LLM serving sees up to 16.8% prefill-energy and 28.7% energy-cost reductions, while autonomous-vehicle perception also improves under real-time latency constraints.

tracking_records.title: Decoupling Readiness from Release for Tail-Aware Scheduling of Agentic LLM Workflows
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / workflow serving scheduler
tracking_records.why: Tail-risk-aware release scheduling jointly controls which ready agent turn to submit and how much unfinished work to expose. On real software-engineering agent traces it remains comparable under light load and reduces P95 workflow flow time under contention by up to 3.50x.

tracking_records.title: IMLE-VLA: Fast Single-Step Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Policies
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / action head / single-step generation
tracking_records.why: Replaces the 10-step flow-matching action head in pi0.5 with a single-step cIMLE generator. Inference frequency rises 15 to 55 Hz (3.67x), action throughput up to 11x, LIBERO average success reaches 98%, and real-robot per-episode VLA inference is 3.9-6.6x faster.

tracking_records.title: REACH: Controller-Managed Long-Span ECC for HBM AI Inference
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / HBM reliability architecture
tracking_records.why: Controller-managed long-span ECC exploits read-dominated LLM decode and known-erasure repair. At the analytical 2.69 TB/s application target, REACH reports 55.8% less controller area and 57.7% less modeled power than the evaluated mean-work direct-long design while preserving 32 B transactions.

tracking_records.title: ExaServe: Large-Scale LLM Serving on Exascale HPC Systems
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / distributed inference / HPC systems
tracking_records.why: A pip-installable framework turns a declarative YAML spec into large-scale LLM serving deployments on leadership-class supercomputers. On ALCF Aurora it scales from 1 to 256 nodes (3072 vLLM replicas), reaching 27.1k requests/s and 3.8M tokens/s for non-streaming inference, while exposing centralized streaming-proxy and Ray Serve control-plane bottlenecks.

tracking_records.title: Composable CXL Memory as a Kubernetes-Native Shared Memory for LLM Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / KV cache / CXL / cloud runtime
tracking_records.why: A Kubernetes DRA driver exposes composable CXL as cross-node shared KV-cache memory for vLLM/llm-d. Cross-node prefix reuse reduces TTFT by 5.5x-36.6x at 95.4-99.5% external hit rates, with only 1-4% sharing gap versus same-node reuse.

tracking_records.title: NCP-ArchPreview Technical Report: Moving towards Latent Space Language Models through Next Concept Prediction
tracking_records.topic: LLM training efficiency / latent-space language modeling / speculative decoding
tracking_records.why: 8.9B NCP-ArchPreview reaches OLMo-3-7B final pretraining loss after only 51.3% of its total training tokens and approaches a parameter-aligned baseline using 85% standard compute. A 17M VQ module enables lightweight domain adaptation, and concept injection improves DFlash2 accepted length 4.17% with negligible overhead.

tracking_records.title: HybridFLow: SDN-Orchestrated Client Partitioning for Hybrid Federated Learning
tracking_records.topic: distributed training / edge-cloud / federated learning / network-aware scheduling
tracking_records.why: Closed-loop SDN orchestration estimates per-client communication time and partitions synchronous versus asynchronous FL clients using network-wide bottleneck visibility. Across multiple topologies it reaches 80% target accuracy 33-40% faster than SmartFLow and cuts average round duration by 30-40 seconds.

tracking_records.title: PACE: Perceived-Latency-Aware Cascading Service Routing and Filler Control for QoE-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Dialogue Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / RAG serving / Physical AI cloud-edge runtime / dialogue systems
tracking_records.why: PACE jointly controls response-source routing, filler content and volatility-aware cache admission and is deployed on a humanoid-robot sales service. On 75k CarQA requests it halves pure-LLM P95 perceived time-to-first-response (0.29 vs 0.53s at c16), reaches 0.41s P95 and 2.4x lower latency than RAG at high load with equal quality, cuts filler calls by 94%, and eliminates stale answers in the reported setup.

tracking_records.title: Stencil Computation at the Intersection of AI and HPC
tracking_records.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / tensor compiler / heterogeneous GPU / HPC-AI convergence
tracking_records.why: Applies AI tensor-compiler abstractions from TinyTC and Triton to an 8th-order 25-point stencil across Intel, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. On Intel B580, TinyTC reaches 15.6 Gpts/s versus 13.5 Gpts/s for PyTorch/Triton under random initialization, with zero-initialized runs reaching 35.8 Gpts/s through hardware memory compression; the study also exposes bandwidth and cache-management effects. This is direct measured compiler/runtime throughput evidence.

tracking_records.title: Decoupled Self-Forcing Distillation for Streaming Talking Head Generation
tracking_records.topic: video/image generation acceleration / streaming diffusion / causal distillation
tracking_records.why: Decouples low-dimensional causal motion generation from a distilled causal diffusion renderer and runs both as parallel streams. Reports 15.4 FPS at 1.3 s latency with no quality degradation, directly addressing streaming generative inference efficiency.

tracking_records.title: One Loop, Two Gains: Can Active Learning win the Lottery for Free?
tracking_records.topic: sparsity/pruning / training efficiency / active learning
tracking_records.why: Integrates iterative magnitude pruning into the retraining loop already required by pool-based active learning, producing sparse deployable models at practically no additional pruning cost. Winning tickets match dense accuracy up to 95% sparsity and can reduce both retraining and acquisition-scoring cost.

tracking_records.title: Deformable Object Manipulation under Partial Observability via Real-Time Full-Shape Estimation
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot world model / real-time control
tracking_records.why: cRVAE replaces expensive online physics identification with a lightweight learned forward model from partial corner observations. It runs about 350x faster than XPBD on rope and over 1500x faster on fabric per forward pass, keeping receding-horizon planning within a 100 ms control budget and demonstrating hardware deployment on Unitree Go2.

tracking_records.title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / private inference / verifiable delegation / heterogeneous offload
tracking_records.why: End-to-end Qwen3-4B prototype delegates dominant matrix-vector products while preserving input privacy and verifiability with virtually no server verification overhead. With one client thread, throughput improves up to 17x with online privacy masks, 45x with precomputed masks, and 44x for verification-only; client-side microbenchmarks with simulated network delay reach 12-157x depending on mode.

tracking_records.title: LiteRAG: Cost-Efficient Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / RAG / retrieval efficiency / context reduction
tracking_records.why: Replaces retrieval-time LLM control with query-conditioned graph exploration and reasoning-chain context construction. On DistComp it cuts per-query latency by over 100x and cost by over 99% versus GraphRAG Global and DRIFT while achieving the best reported overall quality; on UltraDomain it matches LinearRAG quality with about 14x fewer tokens. This is direct measured RAG serving efficiency evidence.

tracking_records.title: Kernel-Managed Shared Memory for System-Wide Personalization
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory / agent runtime / context management
tracking_records.why: AIOS kernel-managed shared memory centralizes retrieval, privacy enforcement, and prompt injection across agents. Across GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B in 1,800 trials, it approaches full-context personalization while using much shorter prompts and reduces end-to-end latency by 15-61%, with corresponding token and inference-cost reductions.

tracking_records.title: SAGE: Semantic-Aware Geographic Error Recovery for AI Data Movement
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / AI interconnect / fault recovery / communication latency
tracking_records.why: Semantic-aware replay architecture distinguishes catastrophic from quantization-like numerical faults and adapts replay restart geography. gem5 Garnet plus ASAP7 evaluation reports 30.1% lower quality-normalized terminal latency than fixed 34-hop recovery, including 28.0% lower mean latency, bounded queues under higher-BER stress, and lower DeiT-S mean/p99.5 latency.

tracking_records.title: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / asynchronous LLM agents / GUI testing / cost-aware tool use
tracking_records.why: Uses history-aware cluster memory, asynchronous intent generation, and hybrid fulfillment that reserves the LLM for complex intents while routing simple intents to a lightweight heuristic. Across 41 Android apps it achieves up to 36.4% higher code coverage while costing less than one eighth of the best pure-LLM baseline, directly addressing LLM-agent latency and cost.

tracking_records.title: Elastoformer: Enabling Dynamic Adaptivity via Elastic Model Transformation
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / elastic inference / pruning / runtime adaptivity
tracking_records.why: SEC 2025 framework converts pretrained ViTs and CNNs into a single elastic family that switches operating modes at runtime rather than maintaining independent models. Experiments report up to 85% FLOP reduction, 50% latency reduction, and 76% memory-overhead reduction; official author repository is public.

tracking_records.title: CLFTv2: Efficient Camera-LiDAR Fusion for Semantic Segmentation via Hierarchical Feature Pyramids
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / multimodal perception / efficient attention / edge inference
tracking_records.why: Replaces global ViT/query-matching fusion with hierarchical shifted-window attention and a lightweight FPN-style decoder. Against a Swin-based Mask2Former adaptation it uses 1.4x fewer GFLOPs and delivers 2.2x higher throughput with comparable overall accuracy while improving vulnerable-road-user recall, giving direct on-vehicle perception efficiency evidence.

tracking_records.title: AMEND: Audited Margins Enable Nonblocking Drops in GPU-PIM LLM Decoding
tracking_records.topic: KV cache/long-context / sparse attention / GPU-PIM / LLM decoding
tracking_records.why: Predicts block-sparse attention decisions from audited prior-step margins so the GPU fetches only predicted survivors while near-bank PIM concurrently checks omitted blocks, avoiding a serial selector on the token critical path. Across LongBench/RULER simulation at batch 8 it preserves near-baseline quality and reports 1.40-3.63x end-to-end decode speedup with 28-66% lower dynamic decode energy over 8K-64K contexts.

tracking_records.title: InstantMimic: A High Performance System for Learning Physics-based Skills in Seconds
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / GPU systems / robotics training
tracking_records.why: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 system that removes fragmented-kernel and CPU-memory bottlenecks by making simulation, environment computation, policy inference, and policy updates one GPU-native execution flow. The resulting end-to-end pipeline trains diverse physics-based imitation skills in seconds and makes LLM-agent hyperparameter search practical; directly relevant to efficient Physical-AI training/runtime systems.

tracking_records.title: HBFSim: Fast and Faithful Simulation of High-Bandwidth Flash Under Real GPU Execution
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / GPU memory hierarchy / simulation / HBF

tracking_records.topic: mixed-precision attention kernel / long-context inference
tracking_records.why: Long-context prefill in large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory traffic because dense self-attention computes quadratic query-key scores. Existing methods either use a uniform low-precision path or select token interactions, leaving spatial precision routing over hardware-aligned score tiles outside fused dense attention. We introduce TileMix, a tile-centric precision-routing kernel that makes numerical precision an executable spatial decision over score-tile groups within fused dense attention. TileMix partitions the attention matrix into hardware-aligned score tiles, packs routing decisions into compact bitmasks, and dispatches each tile group through FP16 or INT8 score computation while both paths update a shared online-softmax state. Scalable precision grouping lets each routing bit govern multiple adjacent key tiles, preserving hardware-aligned compute tiles and compact metadata at long contexts. By routing all legal tile groups, TileMix preserves dense token connectivity, requires no training, and supports grouped-query attention, variable-length batches, and INT8 key/value caches. Across LongEval, LV-Eval, and A100 prefill benchmarks on LLaMA, Qwen, and Vicuna, TileMix recovers long-context quality lost under uniform INT8 and improves prefill throughput over FP16, yielding a controllable accuracy-efficiency frontier across model families. The implementation is available at https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileMix.

tracking_records.title: Global Simulation-Guided Dynamic Operator Scheduling for Efficient Multi-Tenant Model Serving
tracking_records.topic: multi-tenant model serving / operator-level scheduling
tracking_records.why: Container-granularity scheduling leaves abundant short-lived idle slices within containers unexploited. Reallocating containers is too heavyweight to utilize such fine-grained opportunities under SLA constraints, and operator-level scheduling requires reasoning about dependencies, memory safety, and cluster-wide execution dynamics in real time. In this paper, we present SliceScheduler, a dynamic operator-level scheduling system for multi-tenant model serving. The key idea is to expose cluster-wide operator execution state and enable what-if reasoning over scheduling decisions. SliceScheduler consists of four key components. First, we introduce the Global Mapping Graph (GMG), a unified abstraction that captures operator dependencies, tensor shapes, resource mappings, and execution states, providing a real-time, cluster-wide view with explicit resource semantics. Second, we build a global simulator on top of GMG to predict operator-level execution and memory evolution under candidate placements. Third, we design an incremental, simulation-based scheduling module that selects placements to exploit fragmented idle slices while avoiding memory violations and preserving SLA. Finally, we develop an operator executor that materializes scheduling decisions on GPUs and coordinates computation and cross-accelerator transfers. We implement SliceScheduler as a PyTorch backend and evaluate it using production trace replay. Experimental results show that SliceScheduler improves token throughput by 1.10--2.29$\times$ compared to existing approaches, while maintaining SLA violations within 9\%. SliceScheduler demonstrates that operator-level scheduling is a practical and effective approach to improving GPU utilization for multi-tenant LLM serving.

tracking_records.title: Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Efficient VLA Inference via Speculative Inference and Verification
tracking_records.topic: VLA speculative inference / algorithm-architecture co-design
tracking_records.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in the field of embodied AI, but their high computational cost and limited predicted action length hinder real-time deployment. Although Dadu-Corki, a dedicated accelerator for efficient embodied AI, has been introduced, it does not exploit the inherent interaction patterns between the robot and its environment, which results in a relatively short predicted action length. We observe that robotic environments naturally alternate between active states-where precise actions are crucial-and inactive states-where actions have limited impact on task success. This insight enables a new scheduling opportunity: long-action-length speculative prediction in inactive states, paired with selective verification in active states. We propose SpecVLA, an algorithm-system co-design framework that adaptively balances action length, inference latency, and task reliability. On the algorithm side, SpecVLA introduces a state-aware VLA inference execution paradigm and a hardware-friendly construction of a smaller verification model (sVLA) using differential residuals and block-wise mixed-precision quantization. On the system side, we develop a heterogeneous architecture consisting of a GPU and a robotic-specific hardware module, along with a speculative dataflow that decouples VLA and sVLA through parallel execution. Comprehensive evaluations on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill benchmarks show that SpecVLA reduces end-to-end latency significantly while preserving task success rate. By enabling long-action-length speculative prediction with timely verification, SpecVLA achieves real-time robotic manipulation with both high efficiency and reliability.

tracking_records.title: GraniKV: Asymmetric Granularity KV-Cache Paging for Multi-Agent Systems with Long Shared Prefix
tracking_records.topic: KV-cache paging / multi-agent serving
tracking_records.why: Production paged-serving engines apply uniform paging granularity to the KV cache, even though the two regions of a multi-agent workload have opposite storage requirements: a long shared prefix demands contiguity, while the per-request suffix demands fine-grained allocation. We present \textbf{GraniKV}, a KV-cache layer that allocates the shared prefix in a contiguous HOT pool and the suffix in a token-level COLD pool, combined with a per-step dispatcher which selects the appropriate backend among dual backends for each regime (compute-, memory-, or communication-bound). To the best of our knowledge, GraniKV is the first system to apply asymmetric paging granularity to the KV cache of a production paged-serving engine. At $L_p{=}16$\,K shared tokens GraniKV reaches $\mathbf{2.16\times}$, $\mathbf{1.98\times}$, and $\mathbf{1.57\times}$ output-token throughput over the production baseline on Llama-3.1-8B/TP=1, Qwen-2.5-14B/TP=2, and Qwen-2.5-32B/TP=4. The gain decomposes: cascade attention integration contributes the majority at saturation; the asymmetric storage layer adds $1.05$--$1.15\times$ end-to-end while being what makes the batched-GEMM prefix backend possible at all. Under heterogeneous multi-agent serving with \emph{distinct} prompts of different lengths, the attribution inverts: GraniKV sustains $\mathbf{1.95\times}$ while batch-global cascade collapses to parity --- the storage layer alone carries the win in the regime that motivates the paper.

tracking_records.title: EcoVLA: Energy-Efficient Device-Edge Co-Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models under Real-Time Constraints
tracking_records.topic: VLA device-edge co-inference / energy-aware runtime
tracking_records.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising foundation for Embodied AI, but their high inference cost poses significant challenges for deployment in robotic systems. In practice, on-device inference is constrained by limited compute capacity and energy budgets, struggling to simultaneously satisfy real-time control and energy efficiency requirements. Alternatively, offloading the inference workload to an edge server is susceptible to fluctuations in system conditions, introducing unpredictable latency risks. Device-edge co-inference offers a promising solution, but systematic research tailored to VLA models remains scarce, particularly a unified co-inference framework that jointly addresses real-time constraints and system-level energy efficiency. Thus, we propose EcoVLA, an adaptive device-edge co-inference framework for VLA models that maximizes system energy efficiency under real-time constraints. EcoVLA first introduces a unified stage-level abstraction over different VLA paradigms, establishing an architecture-agnostic co-inference design space. It then formulates a joint device-edge-network latency and energy prediction model to enable rapid runtime evaluation of candidate co-inference schemes. Building on this, EcoVLA continuously selects the energy-optimal scheme satisfying real-time constraints with millisecond-level overhead, adapting to runtime variations in network and system states. Furthermore, EcoVLA incorporates a lightweight transmission mechanism for inter-stage intermediate tensors to reduce the communication overhead incurred by cross-device collaboration. Experimental results across VLA models show that EcoVLA improves system energy efficiency by up to 236% over existing co-inference approaches under a 20 Hz action output frequency constraint, while consistently maintaining SLO satisfaction under dynamic network and edge workload conditions.

tracking_records.title: Every Expert Counts: ExactMoE for Memory-Efficient W4A16 Inference
tracking_records.topic: MoE memory-efficient W4A16 inference / GPU slot cache
tracking_records.why: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models reduce arithmetic by activating only a small subset of experts per token, yet deployment still requires storing and moving the full expert bank. We present ExactMoE, an inference design that applies symmetric group-128 four-bit weight quantization only to routed experts, stores those experts in kernel-native MARLIN form in pinned host memory, and executes all selected experts through a configurable GPU-resident slot cache and fused grouped MoE kernels. The router, attention, embeddings, normalization layers, and language-model head remain in BF16. "Exact" refers to complete expert availability and an unchanged top-k routing procedure: no expert is pruned, substituted, or forced to execute on the CPU. It does not imply numerical identity with the BF16 model. On OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct, evaluated on a single NVIDIA L4, a 16-slot configuration reduces peak reserved GPU memory from 14.168 to 1.836 GiB (87.04%) while retaining 81.85% of BF16 decode throughput. A fully resident 64-slot configuration reaches 31.923 tokens/s versus 21.662 tokens/s for BF16 while reserving 4.061 GiB. Across 12,450 zero-shot multiple-choice questions, ExactMoE obtains 70.3534% normalized accuracy versus 70.8996% for BF16, retaining 99.23% of the baseline accuracy. In a matched 16-token ablation, fused grouped execution is 1.97x as fast as a sequential W4 reference. These results identify a practical memory-transfer-throughput frontier for complete-expert MoE inference.

tracking_records.title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems
tracking_records.topic: agentic serving characterization / systems benchmark
tracking_records.why: Agentic applications are shifting AI serving from isolated model inference to long-running workloads in which LLMs coordinate tools, environments, and persistent state. However, the system behavior of these workloads---where latency, cost, and bottlenecks arise---remains poorly characterized, leaving serving systems to rely on assumptions built for conventional inference. We present AgentSysBench, a benchmark suite and measurement toolkit with ten representative agentic applications and unified systems-level instrumentation. Across controlled deployments and production traces, we identify six properties that distinguish agentic workloads from conventional LLM serving: (1) execution is heavyweight and stateful, with non-LLM components dominating latency in 5 of 10 applications and sandbox working-set memory peaking at 28 GB per session; (2) applications compose components with heterogeneous resource affinity---GPU-bound inference, memory-bound retrieval, CPU-bound sandboxes---whose task latencies diverge by up to 32x; (3) bottlenecks shift across requests, models, and deployments; (4) production sessions hold state idle for minutes to hours between active steps; (5) a control-plane tax---auxiliary LLM calls and context overhead from tool schemas and observations---crowds out productive compute and context; and (6) production traces from three applications reveal heavy cross-request redundancy in search queries and web fetches, exposing a large caching opportunity. Four design explorations demonstrate that these findings are actionable: task-aware serving reduces latency by 29--40%, communication-aware placement by up to 4.5x, state offloading reduces memory usage by 4.6x, and tool-result caching removes 35.2% of redundant search calls and saves 19.3% of aggregate search latency.

tracking_records.title: DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding
tracking_records.topic: MoE architecture / small-batch decoding
tracking_records.why: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have been widely adopted in real-time interactive applications such as coding assistants, real-time audio-video interaction systems. To meet the extremely low response latency requirements of these scenarios, practitioners commonly employ small-batch decoding, under which MoE inference becomes memory-bound and is severely bottlenecked by expert weight loading. However, this bottleneck has received limited attention, and existing solutions such as post-training weight compression or fine-grained expert design during pre-training either degrade model accuracy or introduce additional computation and communication overhead. To tackle this issue, we propose DeaMoE, a decoding-efficient MoE architecture, in which the experts are grouped into several departments, and the experts belonging to the same department share most parameters since they come from the same professional field, and additionally each expert contains a few private parameters to reflect its uniqueness. Moreover, we design customized two-stage routing strategy for DeaMoE to avoid redundant loading, under which DeaMoE greatly improves the efficiency during LLM decoding. Compared with vanilla MoE, DeaMoE reduces per-step loaded weights by up to 50.9% and achieves up to 1.33 end-to-end TPOT speedup for the pre-trained 7B model on A40, and up to 2.00x and 1.97x peak speedup for DeepSeek-V3 on A40 and H100 in microbenchmarks.

ReflexBench contains six dynamic tasks and introduces an evaluation framework that decouples simulator stepping from robot control while supporting configurable latency under synchronous and asynchronous inference. Building upon ReflexBench, we propose ReflexVLA, an efficient VLA model designed for reaction-critical manipulation without large-scale robot-data pretraining. ReflexVLA enhances temporal reasoning through latent future prediction and multi-frame temporal fusion within the vision backbone, while reducing deployment latency through batched visual encoding and CUDA Graph replay. Experiments show that ReflexVLA consistently improves dynamic manipulation performance while maintaining competitive accuracy on standard static manipulation benchmarks, and real-world experiments further demonstrate its effectiveness under practical deployment conditions. tracking_records.title: Beyond Capacity: Scalable MoE LLM Inference via High-Bandwidth Flash with Direct GPU and HBM Paths
tracking_records.topic: MoE serving / high-bandwidth flash architecture
tracking_records.why: Modern mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models increasingly strain the capacity and cost efficiency of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as rapidly growing expert weights must be provisioned close to GPUs. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers substantially greater capacity, but conventional designs typically deliver HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through HBM, leaving an additional direct GPU-HBF connection underutilized. We explore an HBF organization that simultaneously exploits two independent expert-delivery routes: a direct path that transfers expert weights from HBF to the GPU and a relay path that transfers them from HBF through the HBM base die to the GPU. Whole experts are assigned to one of the two routes, and transfers over both routes proceed concurrently, increasing aggregate expert-delivery bandwidth without replicating expert weights or introducing a shared relay bottleneck. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. tracking_records.title: TEMPO: Makespan-Aware Expert-Parallel Load Balancing Across Memory- and Compute-Bound Regimes
tracking_records.topic: MoE expert-parallel load balancing / serving
tracking_records.why: In expert-parallel (EP) MoE serving, every layer synchronizes at the slowest GPU. Dispatchers balance token counts (EPLB, LPLB, UltraEP) or activated-expert counts (METRO), assuming expert time is linear in one. Measurements on two datacenter GPU generations show it is neither: below $n^* \approx 156$--$168$ tokens, HBM weight streaming dominates---cost attaches to $activated replicas$, not tokens; above it, grouped GEMM rounds tokens to 128-tile $M$-tiles, so $splitting$ an expert adds padded compute. A max-affine profile $t=\max(a+bG,\,c+βN)$ captures both regimes. Realistic decode batches hold hot experts in the linear regime and cold in the flat $simultaneously$; recorded batches show proxy dispatches differ by $1.4$--$1.6\times$ in modeled block time (p95 up to $1.7\times$), and $which$ proxy wins flips with the regime. We formalize per-batch dispatch as a fixed-charge makespan problem---NP-hard on two fully replicated GPUs, polynomial in degenerate limits---and present TEMPO, a makespan-aware dispatcher solving it in milliseconds off the critical path; its SGLang integration runs out-of-process and fuses dispatch with count collection into one in-graph kernel. Anchored by an 8-GPU Testbed A microbenchmark, TEMPO stays within $1\%$ of the best fixed baseline everywhere and wins by up to $15.5\%$ where regimes mix. End-to-end on Testbed B, Qwen3-235B (inside the win region) gains $4$--$6\%$ throughput and cuts p99 latency by $\sim 15.6\%$; DeepSeek-V3 (outside, communication-dominated) shows only mechanism cost. A phase diagram, not a universal win, is the claim: it predicts both outcomes before deployment.

tracking_records.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
tracking_records.topic: sparse video attention / DiT inference
tracking_records.why: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) incur quadratic self-attention cost over spatiotemporal tokens. Existing training-free sparse attention methods often construct sparse masks from block-level or cluster-level proxy scores, which can obscure fine-grained differences among keys and miss high contribution keys under aggressive sparsity. Moreover, such proxy scores may yield overly concentrated softmax distributions, causing Top-$p$ to retain too few keys for some query clusters. Although a fixed Top-$k$ minimum alleviates this failure mode, a shared value cannot adapt to variations across heads and inputs. To address both limitations, we propose SCOPE, a training-free sparse attention framework that combines 3D-RoPE-aligned key subspace clustering with online per-head Top-$k$ estimation for efficient video-DiT inference. SCOPE partitions post-RoPE keys into temporal, height, and width subspaces, clusters them independently, and aggregates the corresponding centroid scores through lookup tables to obtain per key proxy scores for each query cluster. Building on existing hybrid Top-$p$/fixed Top-$k$ selection, SCOPE derives a head-specific Top-$k$ value online by averaging the initial retained key counts within each head, weighted by query cluster size, and selects additional keys only for query clusters whose initial retained key counts fall below this value. Sparse attention is then computed over the selected original keys and values. Across six model--task configurations, SCOPE consistently outperforms existing training-free baselines in both fidelity and latency, achieving up to a $1.99\times$ end-to-end speedup on 720p HunyuanVideo with $28.46$ dB PSNR relative to dense attention.

tracking_records.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion
tracking_records.topic: diffusion cache policy / video-image generation acceleration
tracking_records.why: Diffusion models have achieved dominant performance in visual generation but suffer from substantial inference overhead. While cache-based acceleration has emerged as a promising solution, existing policies rely on local similarity heuristics, which we identify as being significantly misaligned with final generation quality. This discrepancy stems from the non-uniform propagation and accumulation of errors along the denoising trajectory. To address this, we propose Global-Impact Cache (GCache). We first establish a rigorous theoretical characterization of the error propagation upper bound. Recognizing that this bound can be overly conservative for complex, highly non-convex diffusion models, we further reparameterize the propagation exponent with a Bernstein form and reformulate cache policy search as a bilevel optimization problem. In detail, GCache identifies an optimal reuse policy in the inner objective while aligning the error-weighting function with generation quality loss in the outer objective. This framework effectively reconciles theoretical rigor with empirical performance, learning to prioritize computation where it most impacts visual fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GCache consistently outperforms prior caching strategies on both video and image generation. Notably, on the state-of-the-art Wan2.1 video diffusion model, GCache maintains a 2.17x speedup while significantly enhancing generation quality, reducing LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316.

This is a useful deployment-quality diagnostic rather than a new acceleration method, so it remains watch.

tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / evaluation / failure recovery / robustness

tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / video/image generation acceleration / agent runtime
tracking_records.why: Provides a full multimodal agent runtime with persistent evidence management plus post-training; a 30B-total/3B-active policy approaches a 1T-parameter agent. Relevant active-parameter/runtime lineage, but no direct latency or throughput ratio is given.

tracking_records.title: APEX-RBD: Mixed-Precision Exploration Framework for Hardware-Efficient Robot Dynamics Accelerator Design
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot accelerator / mixed precision / edge hardware
tracking_records.why: Protected Physical-AI hardware-efficiency candidate. Automates mixed-precision design-space exploration for rigid-body-dynamics accelerators and reports up to 1.9x area reduction and 1.8x power savings across robotic platforms; valuable but focused on dynamics hardware rather than learned policy serving.

tracking_records.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / RAG / soft context compression / inference efficiency
tracking_records.why: DEX-Comp directly targets the inference overhead of long retrieved contexts by encoding documents into substantially shorter embedding sequences. Its two-stage recipe first distills correct uncompressed-RAG behavior, then uses RL only on cases the uncompressed system fails. This is highly relevant to serving efficiency, but the primary abstract emphasizes QA quality across retrieval depths and does not provide a measured latency/throughput or token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

tracking_records.title: Large Language Models with At Most One Spike per Neuron
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / energy-efficient LLM / spiking inference
tracking_records.why: A fully time-to-first-spike LLM formulation is scaled to 1.5B parameters and reports extremely sparse event-driven activity with an energy estimate from spike counts. Because the paper explicitly notes this is a proxy under a cost model rather than measurement on neuromorphic hardware, it is preserved as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

tracking_records.title: MomentQuant: an even more minimalist interval method with linear time complexity for time series classification
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / efficient inference / linear-time algorithms
tracking_records.why: MomentQuant replaces exact interval quantiles with Cornish-Fisher approximations, removes the sorting requirement and reduces inference complexity to linear time. The primary abstract reports the optimized Quant implementation is faster than the original and MomentQuant is faster again with only a tiny predictive-performance decrease, making it relevant to lightweight inference; however, no numeric deployment latency/throughput gain is given in the primary abstract, so it remains watch rather than strong.

tracking_records.title: A Schema Bounded Language Model for Refining Robot Policies Without Destabilizing Local Learning
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / hierarchical agent runtime / decentralized robot control
tracking_records.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime work that cleanly separates expensive LLM reasoning from fast local control: LLM inference is confined to round-level policy generation/refinement while a UCB bandit and policy-conditioned Double DQN execute tick-level actions. In the evaluated three-robot simulation, the complete configuration reached all 90 robot-round goals and achieved 42-tick median completion time, 25.0-39.1% lower than alternative configurations. The evidence is simulation-level task efficiency rather than measured inference latency/throughput, so it remains watch.

tracking_records.title: Compact Bellman-Grounded Cognitive Maps for Cost-Aware Navigation
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / navigation memory / compact world representation / cost-aware planning
tracking_records.why: Learns a reusable Bellman-grounded cognitive map with compact coordinate encoding, enabling changing navigation goals without per-goal retraining. On grids up to 1,600 nodes it maintains full success with only 5% mean gap to Dijkstra, while memory growth is sublinear from 400 to 3,600 nodes. It is valuable protected evidence for compact embodied memory, but not a direct VLA/WAM inference accelerator.

tracking_records.why: Encodes multi-timescale temporal information directly in event representations and introduces a recursive approximation for efficient event-by-event updates, reducing reliance on recurrent temporal modeling while preserving detection performance. The primary abstract does not quantify latency, throughput, or energy gains, so it remains a protected Physical-AI watch item.

tracking_records.why: TROVE preserves valid workflow fragments and revises only execution steps invalidated by new runtime evidence, explicitly targeting wasted computation from stale plans and broad replanning.
